subject: Life Skills
title: The Deductible Tradeoff
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Deductible Tradeoff.

hook.text: Raising your car insurance deductible from $250 to $1,000 can cut your premium by up to 40%.

buildup.text: A deductible is what you pay out of pocket before insurance kicks in. Higher deductible means lower premium.

discovery.text: If you rarely file claims, a high deductible saves money over time. You keep more in premiums.

twist.text: But a high deductible means a big bill when disaster strikes. If you can't cover it, you're stuck.

climax.text: Set your deductible at the highest amount you could comfortably pay from savings today.

punchline.text: Match deductible to savings, not to hope.

quiz.question: How should you choose your insurance deductible?
options: Always pick the lowest one available
Set it at the highest you could pay from savings
Choose the same as your monthly premium
